read:research_mech.summary: The stack is a numeric hidden-mechanism benchmark. A Task (research/tasks.py) is one (family, seed) draw of a hidden mechanism plus money rules (income per tick, endowment = 20 ticks of income) and a public goal. Validated tasks also carry a private normalisation: score 0 = holding the defaults, 1 = the oracle's best constant (or piecewise-constant, in regime families) settings. MechVecEnv (research/envs.py) runs N kernel-free MechSim twins in a Python loop. Observations are fixed-width padded and masked float32 vectors (61 dims with the default EnvSpec: 16 gauges, 16 gauge masks, 12 lever settings in [-1,1], 12 lever masks, 5 scalars). Actions are absolute lever settings in [-1,1], and reward = net cents / (endowment/20). The kernel path (research/bridge.KernelMechEnv, rig.* tool calls) gives bit-identical observations: I measured a max difference of 0.0. It costs 0.7 ms/tick against about 65 us in the simulator. Mechanisms come from three independently written engines registered through mechanisms.base.mech_family: scm (rule-compositional causal graph built from motif blocks), abm (agent-based market with 400-600 customers, adaptive incumbents, a social network) and techsys (a queueing pipeline). There are 24 families: train = abm_congestion, abm_utility, abm_wom, abm_duopoly (2 seats), scm_additive, scm_delay, scm_gate; val = scm_delay_gate, scm_invu, abm_trust_gate, abm_commons, abm_complement, tech_pipeline, tech_handoff; test = scm_stock_gate, scm_feedback, scm_regime, abm_network_fx, abm_segments, abm_duopoly_fx, tech_contention, tech_cascade, tech_redundant, tech_lostwork, tech_shared_pool. The split is enforced mainly through seed ranges (train 0..999,999, val from 1,000,000 via eval_tasks, sealed test seeds from a secret salt via research.sealed) and through task-id plus mechanism-fingerprint overlap checks (_Watch) inside lifetime, internalisation and transfer. The family split is only metadata: nothing stops a training stream from drawing val or test families. New families can be defined in-process with a decorator. For scm a recipe dict selects motif blocks; for abm a kind plus rule overrides; for techsys a scenario plus overrides. I registered and validated a custom delay+feedback+stock+regime family in 2.1 s. On your transfer question: protocols.transfer restores the pretrained arm with the learner's own load(), so it carries whatever save() wrote. CAM 7.0's Cam7Learner.save/load carries the AdamW state, ret_stats, rng state and the full source replay buffer (a 192 MB .replay.npy). I measured the exp3 pretrained-arm replay at 100% source-family episodes when adaptation starts and still 52-58% (1056-1184 of 2048) after 120k target steps. The scratch arm trains only on target data, and _meta_step samples replay uniformly. So the reported negative transfer (C-4b) is confounded by replay dilution, not only by priors or plasticity. model_based saves weights and optimiser but no buffer, and meta_np saves weights only. The env maps naturally to entity tokens. Training families have 4-11 levers and 3-10 gauges per task (EnvSpec caps 12/16, configurable). Slot order is seeded and meaningless across worlds. There are no event tokens: a wrapper must derive them. Hidden entities (customers, firms, stages, latent nodes) exist only in private sim.state, sim.info and engine.truth().

interfaces.name: Learner
interfaces.signature: class Learner: name='learner'; kind='abstract'; __init__(self, spec: EnvSpec, seed: int = 0, device: str = 'cpu'); reset_context(self, n: int, which: np.ndarray | None = None) -> None; act(self, obs: np.ndarray, explore: bool = True) -> np.ndarray; observe(self, obs, action, reward, done, next_obs) -> None; update(self) -> dict; freeze(self, frozen: bool = True) -> None; save(self, path: str) -> None; load(self, path: str) -> None; usage(self) -> Usage
interfaces.notes: All arrays are batched [n, ...]. act returns [n, act_dim] in [-1,1]. reset_context clears only episodic state. update returns at least {'updates': int}. Frozen: no update, and stored experience is neither written nor read. save must not include episodic context. Optional state_hash() -> str replaces checkpoint hashing. Keys under VOLATILE_KEYS ('usage', '_usage', 'rng', 'rng_state', 'random_state', 'generator') are ignored by the frozen check. The harness counts env_steps itself; GPU seconds must be reported via usage().

interfaces.name: EnvSpec
interfaces.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True) class EnvSpec: max_levers: int = 12; max_gauges: int = 16; horizon: int = 120; obs_dim = 2*max_gauges + 2*max_levers + 5; act_dim = max_levers; slices gauges, gauge_mask, last_action, lever_mask, scalars
interfaces.notes: Default obs_dim 61: gauges [0:16] symlog(raw reading), 0 when masked and 0 at reset; gauge_mask [16:32]; last_action [32:44] (settings in force, 2*(x-lo)/(hi-lo)-1); lever_mask [44:56]; scalars [56:61] = last_reward (net/money_scale), last_revenue/scale, last_cost/scale, funds/endowment, t/horizon. The horizon field is not used by MechVecEnv (it uses task.horizon).

interfaces.name: MechVecEnv
interfaces.signature: MechVecEnv(tasks: Sequence[Task], spec: EnvSpec | None = None, seat: int = 0, money: bool = True); reset(which=None, tasks=None) -> obs[n, obs_dim]; step(actions[n, max_levers]) -> (obs, reward[n] float32, done[n] bool, {'net_cents': net[n]}); drain() -> list[dict]; lever_mask(); public() -> list[dict]; attributes sims, tasks, _names, _gnames, _lo, _hi, sim_seconds, steps, done
interfaces.notes: A slot whose episode is done is not stepped (reward 0, done True); call reset(which=done, tasks=[...]) to install new tasks. Episode records (drain) carry task, family, seed, engine, transfer, split, net_cents, score, success, score_first_half/second_half, ticks_fallback/idle, funds_end_cents, random_score. Raises ValueError if a task has more levers/gauges than the spec allows. Mixed horizons work, but run_episodes runs until the longest finishes.

interfaces.name: run_episodes
interfaces.signature: run_episodes(env: MechVecEnv, learner, explore: bool = False, learn: bool = False) -> list[dict]
interfaces.notes: One episode per slot; feeds observe only if learn and not frozen; never calls update.

interfaces.name: Task / make_task / build_tasks / eval_tasks / train_stream / families_by
interfaces.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True) Task(family, seed, mech_seed, world_seed, income, endowment, horizon, n_seats=1, validated=False, goal_net_cents=None, default_net=None, reference_net=None, random_net=None, solvable='unknown', rejected=(), engine='', transfer='', split=''); Task.sim(money=True, held=None, funds=None) -> MechSim; Task.world_config(tools=False, holders=('agent',)) -> (cfg, seed); Task.score(net_per_tick); Task.success(total_net_cents); make_task(family: str, seed: int, validate: bool = True, max_tries: int = 8) -> Task; build_tasks(pairs, workers=1, max_tries=8, use_cache=True, skip_failures=False) -> list[Task]; eval_tasks(families, n, split='val', offset=0, **kw) -> list[Task]; train_stream(families, start=0, shuffle_seed=None) -> Iterator[Task]; families_by(split=None, engine=None, transfer=None, seats=1) -> list[str]

interfaces.name: train_pool / pool_stream
interfaces.signature: train_pool(families: Sequence[str], n_per_family: int, start: int = 0, workers: int = 1) -> list[Task]; pool_stream(pool, shuffle_seed=0) -> Iterator[Task]

interfaces.name: protocols.evaluate
interfaces.signature: evaluate(learner, tasks, *, spec=None, n_envs=16, segments=4, explore=False, reset_every=None, verify_frozen=True, label='', cost=None, boot_seed=0) -> dict
interfaces.notes: freeze(True), reset_context per batch, no observe or update, hash of save() before and after, batches bucketed by horizon. Records gain segment_scores, adaptation, slope, rise, ticks_moved, first_move_tick, drift.

interfaces.name: protocols.lifetime
interfaces.signature: lifetime(learner, train_tasks, budget_env_steps, eval_every, eval_sets, *, spec=None, n_envs=16, update_every=1, explore=True, segments=4, checkpoint_dir=None, resume=True, thresholds=(0.5,), sustain=2, budgets=None, require_disjoint=False, verify_frozen=True, label='', on_point=None, max_points=None) -> dict
interfaces.notes: train_tasks can be a list (cycled), a callable index->Task, or an iterable. Training runs whole batches of exactly n_envs tasks of one horizon; update() is called every update_every ticks and at the end of the batch. At each point: frozen eval on every set, then learner.save(point_XXXX.ckpt). Resume calls learner.load(last checkpoint).

interfaces.name: protocols.transfer / transfer_targets
interfaces.signature: transfer(learner_factory, source, targets, *, source_budget, adapt_budget, eval_every, seeds=(0,), spec=None, n_envs=16, update_every=1, segments=4, threshold=0.5, sustain=1, floor=0.0, alpha=0.05, workdir=None, label='') -> dict; transfer_targets(source_families, n_eval=8, split='val', adapt_start=500_000, seats=1, **build_kw) -> {name: {'category', 'families', 'eval', 'train'}}
interfaces.notes: Per seed: learner = factory(seed); _train on the source; learner.save(seed_s/source.ckpt). Per target: pre = factory(seed); pre.load(ck); new = factory(seed). Zero-shot evaluate on both. Then lifetime(pre, target stream) and lifetime(new, same stream) with require_disjoint=True. Reports the AUC difference/ratio, steps to threshold and the negative_transfer flag. What carries into the pretrained arm is whatever save() wrote.

interfaces.name: mech_family
interfaces.signature: mech_family(name: str, engine: str, split: str, transfer: str, doc: str, motifs: tuple[str, ...] = (), seats: int = 1) -> decorator for build(rng: np.random.Generator, overrides: dict) -> dict (params for Engine.generate)
interfaces.notes: split in train/val/test; transfer in base/within/compositional/structural/cross_impl; train requires base. Re-registering a name silently overwrites. make_mechanism(family, seed, overrides) seeds rng from (seed, digest(['mech', family])).

interfaces.name: Engine
interfaces.signature: class Engine: engine: str; generate(cls, rng, params) -> dict; levers(seat) -> list[Lever]; gauges(seat) -> list[Gauge]; brief(seat) -> str; horizon; n_seats; init_state(rng) -> dict[str, ndarray]; step(state, settings: list[dict], rng, t) -> StepResult(state, readings, revenue, cost, score, info); truth() -> dict(nodes, edges, regimes, motifs, ...)
interfaces.notes: Register with @register_engine. step must be pure. Lever(name, lo, hi, default, integer=False). A new engine module is not auto-imported by load_engines (only abm, scm, techsys).

interfaces.name: MechSim
interfaces.signature: MechSim(mech: dict, world_seed: int, rig_id='r1', *, income_cents_per_tick=None, funds=None, held=None, engine=None); reset(); step(settings_per_seat=None) -> StepResult; snapshot() -> tuple; restore(snap); run(policy, ticks) -> dict; attributes t, state, settings, funds, last (per-seat status ok/fallback/idle/empty), info
interfaces.notes: Settings persist between ticks (partial overlay). snapshot/restore gives exact counterfactual forks (verified). Several seats can be driven by passing a list of per-seat dicts.

interfaces.name: scm recipe (build return value)
interfaces.signature: _recipe keys: required: list[block]; pool: {block: weight}; n_blocks: [lo, hi]; kinds: {edge_kind: weight} (default {'linear':4,'saturating':6}); neg_edge_p=0.2; share_p=0.25; series_p=0.3; free_p=0.15; harmful_p=0.5; distractors=[1,2]; gauge_lag_p=0.0; regime=False; latent_noise=[0.005,0.03]; gauge_noise=[0.005,0.04]; horizon=96; seats=1
interfaces.notes: Blocks (blk_*): direct, chain, fork, collider, mediator, gate, threshold, delay, stock, invu, interaction, feedback, confounder (plus dormant, added automatically when regime=True). Edge kinds allowed in 'kinds': linear, saturating, threshold, invu, delay (not product: product needs src2 and would crash). seats>1 adds lag-1 coupling between seats. Unknown keys are silently dropped. handmade(levers, latents, outcome, gauges=None, exogenous=None, price, units, overhead, horizon, regime_at, income_cents_per_tick) builds a hand-specified mechanism dict.

interfaces.name: abm generate overrides
interfaces.signature: build returns {'kind': one of utility|wom|congestion|trust_gate|network_fx|segments|duopoly|commons|complement|duopoly_fx, plus optional n_customers (50..20000), n_seats, n_inc, horizon, noop, net{kind ring|pa|blocks, ...}, p0, flip, rules{wom, congest, gate, nfx, bundle, commons, sigma, phi, delta, tau, price_lag, ...}, pop{...}, cost{...}, seat{...}, adapt{...}, inc{...}}
interfaces.notes: A new kind needs entries in module-level _KINDS, _CHAINS and _GOOD (truth() and roles() index them), so only rule recombination of existing kinds is clean. Levers are dials 0..100 with seeded direction flips.

interfaces.name: techsys generate overrides
interfaces.signature: build returns {'scenario': pipeline|contention|cascade|redundant|lostwork|handoff|shared_pool, plus optional horizon, ages, substeps, period, arrivals, amp, drift, burst_on, burst_x, deadline, settle, lag, default_loss, default_margin, stages, batch_stages, distractors, intake, hide (gauge kinds to leave out), no_calibration}
interfaces.notes: Values are numbers or [lo, hi] ranges. The 'hide' option gives partial observability by gauge kind.

Transfer contamination, exp3 cam7_small seed 0: source.ckpt.replay.npy is 191,845,180 bytes, 1,984 source episodes (versions 0-60). Source-era episodes in the pretrained arm's replay at points 0-4 (0, 30k, 60k, 90k, 120k adapt steps): compositional 1984/1984, 1824/2048, 1600, 1408, 1184 (58% at the end). Within ends at 1056 (52%), structural at 1088 (53%), cross_impl at 1184 (58%). The scratch arm's replay holds only target episodes (864-992 at the end). The AdamW state (100 param states) also carries over.
gotchas: Negative-transfer confound: protocols.transfer restores the pretrained arm through learner.load(source.ckpt). Cam7Learner.load restores the replay buffer, the AdamW moments, ret_stats, rng state and the version counter. _meta_step samples replay uniformly, so 89% (at 30k) and still 52-58% (at 120k) of the pretrained arm's meta-training draws source-family episodes, while the scratch arm trains 100% on target. This favours 'within' (same families; C-4a passed) and penalises the compositional, structural and cross_impl targets (C-4b-d failed). A clean rerun needs the pretrained arm to drop replay (and ideally optimiser state) on load, or the scratch arm to get a matched replay.

The baselines save different state: model_based saves net + Adam but no buffer; ppo saves net + Adam + ret_var; meta_np saves weights only. Transfer comparisons across learners therefore do not carry the same state.

Family splits are metadata. train_stream, task_stream, make_task and train_pool accept val or test families. eval_tasks(split='val') only checks the split argument, so it builds test-family tasks at val seeds too. Only research.sealed restricts to test families. Overlap guards (_Watch) compare task id and mechanism fingerprint, never family membership.

Custom families registered in-process (like cam7.worlds) are unknown to build_tasks/train_pool worker processes (multiprocessing 'spawn' imports only the built-in engines): use workers=1, or a worker initializer that imports your module.

The task and train_pool caches are keyed by (TASK_VERSION, CONTRACT_VERSION, engine, family name, seed), not by the recipe. Editing a custom family's build function under the same name silently returns stale cached tasks. Rename the family or point CRUCIBLE_CACHE elsewhere.

Kernel world families mech_<F> are registered by worldgen.mech_families.register_mech_world_families(). Call it again after registering a custom family, or Task.world_config() / KernelMechEnv will not find it.

scm recipe: unknown keys are silently ignored; 'product' must not be in 'kinds' (it needs src2: a KeyError); the 'regime' flag auto-adds a dormant block and changes the best path's weight at a hidden tick in [0.4, 0.6]·horizon. Calibration can fail (up to 40 internal redraws), and validity can then reject the draw (max_tries redraws in sample_valid, ValueError if all fail).

The observation carries no lever ranges, integer flags, names or horizon. Defaults are visible only as last_action at t=0. Gauges are 0 at reset (no reading yet). last_action shows the desired settings even on fallback ticks, when the sim actually ran at defaults (MechSim.settings is not overwritten by settle_tick's 'used'). The status (ok/fallback/idle) is only in sim.last and the episode counters.
Slot order of levers and gauges is the mechanism's seeded public order and means nothing across worlds; abm dials may run backwards (flip). Do not learn slot-specific weights.
Reward = net cents / (endowment/20) = net / income per tick, so magnitudes are tiny (the ledger reports per-tick sd 0.002-0.06). Normalise per task.
Score 1 = the oracle's best constant (piecewise in regime families) settings, so scores above 1 are possible. default_net, reference_net and random_net are private: never feed them to a learner.

protocols batches tasks by equal horizon (TaskSource buckets), so training batches are single-horizon. run_episodes and MechVecEnv with mixed horizons keep stepping the batch until the longest episode ends (finished slots idle).

MechVecEnv drives one seat. In multi-seat tasks the other seats are 'empty' and run at defaults, so there is no competing learner. families_by and transfer_targets default to seats=1, which drops 2-seat families (abm_duopoly train; abm_commons, abm_complement, tech_handoff val; tech_shared_pool, abm_duopoly_fx test).
No techsys family is in train; all are cross_impl. tech_pipeline is the only 1-seat val techsys family.
VAL offsets 60,000 (dev), 70,000 (C-2/C-3) and 80,000 (C-4) are spent per the ledger; offset 0 (1,000,000+) is the long-inspected dev set. New confirmations need a fresh offset.
x2_confound_gate uses the confounder and feedback motifs of the sealed test family scm_feedback. Tuning on it leaks knowledge of test-family structure (not seeds).
lifetime evaluates only at batch boundaries and resets context. learner.save is called at every point, so for CAM7 every point writes a 190 MB replay file (disk use).
reuse_recommendations: Use MechVecEnv plus train_pool as the fast inner-loop world (about 5k env-steps/s single-process on the mixed training families). Parallelise across processes yourself; the env loops over tasks in Python, one process, with no vectorisation inside.

Use KernelMechEnv (or Task.world_config(tools=True) for the code/cloud/workflow variant) as the bridge from numeric control to real Crucible tool calls. It is bit-identical, so a numeric policy can be validated in the sim and then executed as tool calls in OpenWorld.

Wrap observations as tokens. Lever tokens: setting, mask, plus range/integer/default from task.sim().engine.levers(seat), which is public via rig.spec. Gauge tokens: symlog value and delta. Global token: the five scalars. Event tokens built by the wrapper from consecutive steps: setting changes, net/revenue/cost, funds, status from sim.last. Give per-episode random identities instead of slot IDs (as CAM7 does). Counts vary per task (4-11 levers, 3-10 gauges); raise EnvSpec.max_levers/max_gauges if new families need more.

For world-model auxiliary targets and diagnostics, use MechSim.snapshot/restore (exact counterfactual forks), StepResult.info and engine.truth(). These are operator-side: never feed them as inputs at evaluation.

Make diverse worlds with new mech_family registrations rather than new engines. Delays, stocks, lagged gauges: scm blocks delay/stock and gauge_lag_p, techsys lag/settle. Feedback: scm feedback, abm wom/congestion, techsys cascade. Resource constraints: funds/fallback built in, techsys shared pool, abm capacity/commons. Regime changes: scm regime=True, techsys cascade/redundant, abm endogenous exit/entry. Network effects: abm net + nfx/wom rules, scm seats>1 coupling. Partial observability: scm gauge subsets, noise, pure-noise gauges; techsys hide. Competing agents: abm adaptive incumbents; for learned opponents, drive multi-seat MechSim directly. Put the families in one importable module, validate with T.make_task(..., validate=True) (about 2 s per scm task), use workers=1 or an initializer, and give each recipe version a new family name.

Keep protocols.evaluate, lifetime and transfer as the measurement harness (frozen check, disjointness, paired stats). For transfer, implement CAM Unified's save/load so the pretrained arm does not inherit source replay, or add an explicit 'adaptation reset' hook, and report both variants. Keep weights-only and weights+optimiser variants as ablations.
Use model_based (learners.make('model_based')) and exact regression (meta_np untrained) as the bars to beat. Per the ledger, held-out scores are 0.164-0.242 for these and 0.180 for CAM 7.0.
Draw training tasks only from TRAIN seeds (train_pool or task_stream) and evaluation tasks only from eval_tasks with a fresh offset. Always pass require_disjoint=True to lifetime.
gaps: No semantic or text observations and no executable-code actions in MechVecEnv: actions are 12 continuous lever settings. Tool calls and code exist only through the kernel bridge and the mech_<F>_tools world families (not batched).

No event-token or entity-token interface in crucible: event tokens must be built by a wrapper (CAM7's _Episode/history_batch is one implementation in superlearner). Hidden entities (customers, firms, stages) are not exposed except through private state and truth.
No multi-agent learning interface: MechVecEnv controls one seat, and multi-seat tasks leave the others empty at defaults. Learned competing agents need a custom MechSim driver.
No lifetime-memory or continual-learning protocol beyond internalisation(..., retention=...) (two families in sequence); no multi-domain sequential-retention benchmark and no distributed actors.

The transfer protocol has no option to strip replay or optimiser state from the pretrained arm. Its checkpoint semantics are entirely the learner's save/load, which confounds CAM 7.0's negative-transfer result.
Family-level split enforcement is missing: nothing refuses training on val or test families. A guard would have to be added in CAM Unified's own harness.
Registering a custom family is process-local and not picked up by spawn workers or the kernel worldgen without extra calls; new abm kinds need edits to module-level dicts (_KINDS, _CHAINS, _GOOD).
There is no vectorised or GPU environment: throughput is CPU-bound Python, about 3k env-steps/s for abm and about 15k for scm per process.
There is no train_pool in tasks.py (it is in research/learners/training.py); tasks.py has train_stream.

read:ow_agent_api.summary: Crucible OpenWorld 4.0 (crucible/src/crucible) is an event-sourced, single-threaded, fully headless Python kernel (core/kernel.py `World`). Tool calls run as transactions that emit hash-chained events tagged with a visibility `vis` ("public", a tuple of principals, or "internal" for evaluator-only). Simulated time moves only through `advance_time(until)`, which runs the scheduled processes: consumers, billing, firm minds, rig ticks. A tool's `cost_s` is bookkeeping and never moves the clock by itself. All agent access goes through `crucible.api.WorldServer` (api/local.py). Operator calls: `create_world`, `join_world`, `advance_time`, `snapshot_world`/`fork_world`, `replay_events`, `evaluate_world`, `world()`. Actor calls take a bearer token or an `ActorIdentity`: `observe`, `available_tools`, `execute_action`. Gym (`CrucibleEnv`), PettingZoo (`CrucibleParallelEnv`), FastAPI (OpenEnv /reset /step /ws, MCP POST /mcp, REST /v1) and a stdio MCP server are thin adapters over it. The existing experiments mostly skip WorldServer: they drive the kernel directly through `agents.base.Runner`, one action per agent per round followed by `advance_time(now+dt)`, with `Policy.act(obs_dict, tools) -> {"tool","args"} | None`. That is how `research.llm_eval.run_open_economy`/`run_mechanism`, `evaluation.harness.run_goal` and the CAM2 `integrations.agentrs_cam2.CrucibleAdapter` work. Observations are JSON plus deterministic text. WorldServer returns an `Observation` dataclass: time, seq, compact visible events since the actor's cursor (its own cmd records hidden), per-module summaries (`Module.observe(world, actor)`: own bank balances, orgs, mail unread, rig seat readings), last_result, and the tool list when it changed. `obs.text` is that rendered by `api.render.render_observation`; on the first observation it includes the whole tool list, 20.8k chars for ow_tiny (145 tools) and 28k chars for ow_market (200 tools). There is no HTML unless the optional web module is used. Tools are MCP-shaped `{name, description, inputSchema (strict JSON-schema subset, additionalProperties false), annotations {readOnlyHint, costSeconds, host, builtin, version}}`. The action is `{"tool": "<host>.<endpoint>", "args": {...}, "idempotency_key"?: str}`, and `parse_action` also accepts model text (code fences, `<tool_call>`, OpenAI/MCP shapes). The result is `{ok, t, tool, cost_s, result | error{code,message,details}}`. Rejected calls never raise and come back with structured hints (near-miss names, schema paths). Writing code is ordinary tool use: `code.create_repo` -> `code.commit {files: {path: source}}` -> `code.run {target: "file.py:fn"}` or `cloud.rent` + `cloud.deploy` (crucible.json manifest) + `market.list`. Code runs in a Landlock+seccomp process sandbox, which is available on this host and takes about 90 ms per run. OpenWorld families (worldgen/ow_families.py: ow_tiny, ow_market, ow_frontier, ow_composite, ow_heldout, ow_works) are registered only by `crucible.load_all_modules()`. Their hidden rules (category wire formats, latent and derived demand, mechanism config, firm tiers) live in `World.spec` and state and are evaluator-only. Rewards are not native to the world: they come from operator-side objects (`goals.contracts.RewardContract`/`GoalVerifier`, with potential shaping and daily checks, so reward is sparse), and `evaluate_world` has no OpenWorld hook. Measured on this host: an idle simulated hour takes about 5 ms in ow_tiny, about 15-17 ms in ow_market/ow_frontier, and about 8 ms in ow_tiny with an active deployed service. Ordinary tool calls take about 0.1 ms and sandboxed code.run/cloud.deploy about 85-90 ms. Full 8-day open-economy episodes (192 hourly turns) took 0.95 s idle and 2.0 s with the ExampleInductor, which succeeded on day 4. There is no in-process vectorised kernel env for the economy. Fast paths are `research.envs.MechVecEnv` (kernel-free hidden-mechanism simulators, measured 6,046 ticks/s for 32 envs), process-parallel `scale.WorldPool`, and the async `scale.RolloutFarm` with versioned parameter publishing. Cheap episodic resets come from snapshot+fork (5-18 ms). Partial observability is enforced by API discipline: actor operations filter events with `World.visible` plus the `principals_of` hook, hide `admin.*`, and expose only per-actor summaries. An in-process agent could read `World.state`/`spec`, and the REST `GET /v1/worlds/{w}` leaks family+seed to actors, which is enough to regenerate the hidden rules.

Native API minimal loop:
import crucible; crucible.load_all_modules()   # REQUIRED for ow_* families
from crucible.api import WorldServer
from crucible.worldgen import generate
srv = WorldServer('memory://', lease_ttl_s=None)

gotchas: ow_* families exist only after `crucible.load_all_modules()` (it imports worldgen.ow_families). Otherwise generate/create_world raises a KeyError (not an ApiError), so the HTTP server answers 500.

Time never moves on its own. A tool's `cost_s` is only recorded in the principal's time_used. The clock moves through `advance_time`, which is operator-only (REST /advance needs the operator token). Runner/CrucibleEnv advance a fixed dt per round; WorldEnv advances cost_s + think_s; the MCP stdio server needs --advance-dt.

Rate limit: ow families set params.max_actions_per_hour=240. More calls inside one simulated hour come back as `rate_limited`, which matters for a fast learner that makes many calls between clock advances.

Rewards are not part of the world. Use RewardContract (potential shaping plus daily checks), which is ~0 on most steps and changes at daily checks: sparse. WorldServer.evaluate_world has no OpenWorld hook and returns only invariants, counts and the digest.

Observation.last_result persists across later observations until the next action ('last action: X' keeps showing after time advanced; EvalLLMPolicy strips that line). Own cmd/cmd.rejected events are hidden (hide_own_commands=True). Events beyond max_events are dropped oldest-first and reported in `dropped`.

The first observation (and any observation after the tool list changes) embeds the whole catalogue: 20-28k chars. Use include_tools='never' plus discovery.render_catalogue / world.find_tools for a budget.
The action space is dynamic. Agent-deployed services (`<host>.solve`) become tools only after the actor discovers the host (world.describe, search.query results, ads). Watch tools_changed/new_tools.

Two observation formats coexist. WorldServer gives an `Observation` dataclass (summary, events, text). Runner/ActorView/WorldEnv give a dict = World.observe(actor) + 'events' + 'events_dropped'. render_actor_observation handles both.
Fork-mode CrucibleEnv: base_snapshot defaults to the world state at env construction, the episode world id changes every reset (info['world_id']), and the clock continues from the snapshot time.

Separation of hidden state is by API discipline only. In-process code can read World.state, World.spec (category seeds, hidden wire-format rules, rig mechanism config, consumer latent/derived edges, firm tiers) and call World.query/system_call. CAM Unified must use only actor operations.

Leak: REST GET /v1/worlds/{w} (allowed for actors) returns world_info including family and seed. With them `crucible.worldgen.generate(family, seed)` reproduces every hidden rule. The redteam suite treats the world seed as secret, yet this route exposes it.

Builder/deployed_service_prefix use privileged knowledge (economy.needs `tier_source(need, best_tier(need))` reference solvers). They are feasibility witnesses, not fair demonstrations. ExampleInductor is the non-privileged competent control (public use.examples only).
world.validate checks only the tool name and argument schema (not permissions, existence, funds). For example rig.set with an unknown lever validates true and is rejected at execution.

WorldServer takes a store lease per world (lease_ttl_s=600). A second server on the same sqlite/postgres world gets ConflictError, and a crashed holder blocks others until the lease expires. Use lease_ttl_s=None in tests.
goals.contracts.instantiate builds a World with no store. World.snapshot() then raises (needs a store); use snapshot_blob()/World.from_blob.

Determinism (fork == parent, cross-process equality) holds only under params.cost_model='deterministic', which all ow_* families set. Sandboxed outputs are recorded in internal `ext` events so replay does not re-run code.
Deployed-service calls return ok=true even when the service failed; the HTTP-like status (200/402/500/503) is inside result.

CrucibleEnv observation text is sanitized to printable ASCII ('?' replaces other characters) and cut to max_text_length=65536. The CrucibleEnv default dt=60 s is too small for the economy; experiments use 3600.
AsyncRunner advertises batched decisions (batch_group.act_batch), but no policy in the repo implements it; LLMPolicy makes one HF generate call per turn.
reuse_recommendations: Make WorldServer actor operations (observe / available_tools / execute_action with a token) the only door CAM Unified uses into the world. Keep RewardContract/GoalVerifier, metrics, usefulness_report, Task private fields and World.state on an operator/evaluator side the learner process cannot import from, or run the agent behind make_app's /v1 or /mcp and remove seed/family from the actor-visible world_info.

Use the canonical action JSON {'tool','args'[,'idempotency_key']} and the result {ok,t,tool,cost_s,result|error{code,message,details}} as CAM Unified's action/outcome schema. render.parse_action already accepts model text in many shapes, and error `details` (suggestions, schema paths) are a ready supervised signal for repairing invalid actions.

For the world-model target, use the actor-visible stream: events (type/payload), summary deltas (bank balances, rig readings) and action results. integrations.obs_features (512-d hashed) and EntityMemory/ActionTemplates are parameter-free baselines for the numeric and pointer channels.

Use snapshot_world + fork_world(ephemeral=True), 5-18 ms, for cheap episodic resets and operator-side counterfactual checks of the learned world model: fork, apply an action, compare the prediction with the actual next observation.

For lifetime/continual learning, use reset_mode='continue' worlds on a sqlite store (`WorldServer('sqlite:///...')`): actor cursors and tokens persist, reload with hash verification takes about 0.5 s per 7.7k events, and per-hour cost matches memory://.

For throughput, run worlds in RolloutFarm workers (params published as bytes, per-trajectory param_version and staleness) or WorldPool. Use MechVecEnv (about 6k ticks/s per process for 32 envs) to pretrain the numeric world model on hidden mechanisms; research.bridge transfers the same learner to rig.* tool calls.

Use research.llm_eval.run_open_economy / open_economy_goal and run_mechanism as the evaluation harness: they return diagnosis, interface audit and transcripts. Use the ExampleInductor (non-privileged) and RigExperimenter as competent references, Builder/SchedulePolicy only as privileged ceilings.
For prompts, reuse EvalLLMPolicy.build_messages (v4 interface: discovery.render_catalogue with budget, results with structured errors, history) instead of the raw obs.text.

Start development on ow_tiny (5 ms per simulated hour, 145 tools) and ow_works (economy plus a hidden-mechanism facility: two unrelated ways to earn). Move to ow_market/ow_frontier (15-17 ms per hour, 200 tools, firm minds, founders) and hold out ow_heldout.
gaps: No native structured numeric observation for economy (ow_*) worlds. Only JSON summaries, events and text exist, plus a hashed obs_features helper. The fixed-size numeric observation and action vectors exist only for rig mechanisms (MechVecEnv/EnvSpec).

No in-process vectorised or batched env over kernel economy worlds: each World is single-threaded, so batching means processes (WorldPool/RolloutFarm). No batched LLM decision path exists: AsyncRunner.batch_group is unimplemented and the HFBackend generates one prompt at a time.
No dense intrinsic reward or world-model target API. RewardContract is sparse (daily checks), and evaluate_world has no OpenWorld evaluator hook.
No actor-controlled waiting or clock (e.g. 'sleep until event X'). advance_time is operator-only, so a CAM Unified runtime must own the clock policy itself (fixed dt, cost-based, or event-driven).
No agent-side persistent memory or knowledge store in the API beyond the per-actor event cursor, last_result and tool names. Lifetime memory must be built by CAM Unified.
No compact or budgeted observation option in WorldServer.observe: tool lists are all-or-nothing (include_tools). render_catalogue budgeting has to be applied by the client.
No explicit hidden-state firewall for in-process agents: World.state/spec/query are reachable, and actor-visible world_info leaks family+seed (enough to regenerate hidden rules).

No trained CAM checkpoint on this machine for ow_cam_baseline.py (runs/cam2 missing). The CAM2 adapter has never been trained on Crucible: the report records 0/8 goals, with the controller choosing the first tool with schema-rejected arguments.

No calibrated/real-world dynamics: 37 of the 55 fidelity-register mechanisms are plausible hypotheses, 18 known-unrealistic, none calibrated. Every successful strategy so far is scripted, so no learned positive control exists on open-economy tasks.

read:superlearner_reuse.summary: The repo has two separate learner lineages, and neither one is a CAM Unified prototype. (1) The numeric CAM 6.1/7.0 learners: superlearner/src/superlearner/unified/ (CAM 6.1; the package name is misleading) and cam7/ (CAM 7.0). They run on Crucible's research MechVecEnv, a lever/gauge mechanism world, through the crucible.research.learner.Learner contract (reset_context/act/observe/update/freeze/save/load). (2) Superlearner 4.0: cam/, algo/, train/, world/, grounding/, llm/, continual/, meta/, selfplay/. This is a tool-calling agent for the Crucible 4.0 OpenWorld economy (crucible.core World via world/core.py SessionCore), with a frozen Qwen LLM and a trainable 384-d transformer+GRU controller trained by recurrent PPO. feat/superlearner-4 is merged (merge commit 3e776e7; both the local and origin branches are ancestors of HEAD). origin/feat/async-selfplay (tip 96ed0ee) is also an ancestor of HEAD, so its code is already on this branch under src/agentrs/selfplay and src/agentrs/capacity. It touches only agentrs, not superlearner or crucible. The T_MAX = 256 lifetime cutoff is in cam7/agent.py:33. _Episode preallocates [T_MAX] numpy arrays, and ingest() silently returns once rows >= T_MAX (line 76). history_batch and _sample_cuts also truncate to T_MAX. The FIFO replay is in Cam7Learner.observe (cam7/agent.py:297-298) with Cam7Config.replay_episodes = 2048 (cam7/config.py:63). The actor-critic only uses the last recent_episodes = 96. Cam7Learner.save/load restores the optimizer, numpy RNG, ret_stats, version and the whole pickled replay (.replay.npy). tests/cam7/test_model.py asserts that replay is restored. Crucible's protocols.transfer calls pre.load(source_ckpt), so CAM 7.0's Exp 3 adaptation-from-source carried source replay and Adam moments. That is the contaminated transfer comparison the spec refers to. The other caps: unified EpisodeReplay (per-family uniform reservoir, default capacity 400 per family; UnifiedLearner passes 1500), recent deque(maxlen=100), holdout deque(maxlen=128), and sample_episodes(max_ticks=256). SL4 PPO keeps a FIFO of successes only (replay_episodes = 1500). ContinualPPO keeps a per-arm reservoir of successes only (per_arm 120) plus a world-model buffer of the last 400 episodes. EpisodicMemory (capacity 4000) evicts the oldest failure first. No durable append-only event archive, ANN retrieval index or embedding versioning exists. The closest things are the JSONL fsync episode sink in agentrs Collector and EmbStore.replace / TextBackbone.version. No RMSNorm or SwiGLU exists anywhere in the repo, apart from inside HF Qwen. Every backbone is nn.TransformerEncoderLayer (pre-LN, GELU) or a GRU. There is a correct, tested V-trace (unified/learning/returns.py), along with lambda returns, duration-aware discounting and a per-family return normaliser. There are two PPOs: SL4 recurrent PPO with GAE, KL early stop and rollback (algo/ppo.py), and CAM 7.0's clipped importance-weighted actor-critic over decisions. Both apply ratios to replayed data without validating the estimator. The world models are: SL4 cam/worldmodel.py (one-step MLP on controller state: ok, failure class, reward, next-context, gain), a DreamerV3-style RSSM with slot memory in unified/core/rssm.py (the ledger shows it loses a cue within 4 steps, so avoid it), the causal windowed EventCore, and CAM 7.0's auxiliary heads. The genuinely reusable infrastructure is: SessionCore plus the trusted env server (serve/RemoteCore/spawn_env_server), which is very fast (under 1 ms per decision, about 0.3-0.7 s per simulated day); the async InferenceEngine/Collector pattern (generic act_fn; it currently discards an episode when the policy version changes); SL4 RolloutPool (synchronous, multiprocess); the GPU-aware job queue; plasticity instruments; tensors-only weight export with a fresh-process evaluator (the best template for load_weights_only); the trainable Qwen3 TextBackbone with LoRA/top-k/full modes and an exact gradient cache; the exact NIG posterior with knowledge gradient; and the streaming EpisodeRegression. Distributed infrastructure is missing: there is no multi-GPU or multi-node learner and no actor/learner with off-policy correction. Only one A6000 (49 GB) is present.

key_files.role: Cam7Learner (CAM 7.0 Crucible Learner). Holds T_MAX=256 (line 33), _Episode fixed buffers, FIFO replay trim (297-298), clipped actor-critic _rl_step, save/load that restores opt+rng+replay (439-458). AVOID as a base; mine it for the decision-record schema.
Cam7Config frozen dataclass; replay_episodes=2048, recent_episodes=96, meta_ks=(0..64), d_model 256/4 layers (small: 128/2).

Cam7Model: lever/gauge/global/event tokens, nn.TransformerEncoder (pre-LN GELU) used twice (before and after posterior), learned features, KG + residual decision, value head, world auxiliaries. Specific to the 12-lever/16-gauge MechVecEnv.

Exact batched normal-inverse-gamma regression (Cholesky, float64), Student-t predictive, Thompson sampling, knowledge gradient, info gain. Tested (6 tests pass). Refits from the whole history each call.
duration_discount, lambda_returns, vtrace (Espeholt 2018, duration-aware), ReturnNormalizer (per-family). Tested. IMPORT.
EpisodeReplay: per-family uniform reservoir + recent deque + 10% holdout deque(128); sample() into ReplaySequence; sample_episodes(max_ticks=256). In-RAM only, no persistence.
UnifiedTrainer (CAM 6.1): separate AdamW per group (world/actor/critic/generator/adapt), V-trace actor, twohot critic, AWR program generator, state_dict holds model+opt+norm+counters.
EventCore: causal attention over the last `window` events, no absolute positions (acting = training), direct current-event path, FeatureNorm output.
FeatureNorm (running stats, never same-batch), ObservationEncoder (numeric tokens value/delta/present/id + optional text projection + query compression), GoalEncoder, ActionEncoder (program tokens).
EpisodeRegression: streaming decayed sufficient statistics (A,b) Bayesian linear regression (known noise), ALPaCA-style prefix_nll meta-training. Tested.
DreamerV3-style RSSM + SlotMemory. The ledger shows the transition loses a cue by delay 4. AVOID.
symlog/symexp, twohot encode/loss/mean, unimix, straight-through categorical, balanced KL. Tested; constants checked against DreamerV3.
UnifiedLearner (name 'cam61'): Crucible Learner wrapper; save() writes trainer state (model+opt+norm), NOT replay; load restores optimizer.

SessionCore: the trusted OpenWorld session protocol (info/observe/tools/execute/wait/end_decision/summary), Evaluator (potential-based reward on authoritative state), serve()/RemoteCore/spawn_env_server for sandboxed learners with budgets and a trusted results file. IMPORT.
TaskSpec, disjoint seed/world-family splits (train/curriculum/select/final), build(), task_list(), sealed final list (lock_final/load_final), assert_disjoint. IMPORT.
Env hub over a unix socket (serve_hub/start_hub) so that rollout workers never hold a world.
RolloutPool: multiprocess CPU workers, each with a controller copy; set_weights/set_table/set_wm/sync/run(jobs). Synchronous lock-step collection.
SL4 Trainer: checkpoint = weights+algo/opt+emb store+memory+library+curriculum+rng+counters; replay in a .replay.pkl.gz sidecar; load(weights, memory, optimizer) flags.

export_weights() (tensors-only file + digest) and fresh_eval_main() (new process asserts only weights are loaded, and that memory/replay/tools/embedding cache are empty). Best template for load_weights_only.
param_change, state_of, weights_digest, effective_rank, diagnostics (dormant units, rank, grad/weight norms), probe_fit (plasticity probe).
SL4 recurrent PPO with GAE over whole episodes, KL early stop, rollback with LR halving, SIL replay of successes (FIFO 1500).
ContinualPPO: per-arm success reservoir (120), world-model replay buffer (last 400), parameter groups, anchors/EWC-Fisher, l2init, shrink-perturb.
TextBackbone (Qwen3-0.6B truncated, modes none|lora|top:k|full), LoRALinear, LiveTable gradient cache (exact parameter grads with bounded memory), EmbedService.

InferenceEngine: asyncio dynamic batching over a generic act_fn on one GPU thread, bounded queue, version stamping, stats (from the merged feat/async-selfplay).

Collector: N async logical workers, a dedicated env thread per worker, timeouts, failure containment, fsync'd JSONL episode sink; discards an episode when the policy version changes. Coupled to agentrs.econ.
Function-preserving LoRA rank expansion, expert adapters with a router, distillation, ExpansionAdvisor (for HF LoRA policies).

gotchas: Name collision: the package superlearner.unified is CAM 6.1 (its docstring says so; learner name 'cam61'). Do not put CAM Unified there, and do not assume anything in it is the 'unified' architecture the spec means.

T_MAX truncation is silent: _Episode.ingest returns without error, history_batch truncates, and _Episode preallocates T_MAX rows. It never triggered on 96-120-tick MechVecEnv episodes but would on any OpenWorld lifetime. Cam7 also rebuilds the whole history tensor and refits the posterior at every decision (O(T) per decision). A streaming design must replace this, not just raise the constant.

Other fixed caps: EpisodeReplay.sample_episodes(max_ticks=256) truncates adaptation meta-training to the first 256 ticks; holdout deque(maxlen=128); recent deque(maxlen=100); Cam7 RL uses only the last 96 episodes; SL4 PPO buffer is replay_episodes=1500 FIFO of successes only; ContinualPPO world-model buffer keeps the last 400 episodes; EpisodicMemory capacity 4000; ActorView max_events=30 per observation (events_dropped reported); CAMAgent context uses the last 12 steps.

Checkpoint contamination: Cam7Learner.load restores the Adam state, numpy RNG, ret_stats, version and the full replay. Crucible protocols.transfer does pre.load(ck) before adaptation, so CAM 7.0 Exp 3 'from source' runs carried source replay and optimizer moments. UnifiedLearner.save omits replay but restores the optimizer. The SL4 Trainer._load always restores curriculum, RNGs and counters, even with weights=True, memory=False.

Every checkpoint path uses pickle: torch.load(..., weights_only=False) and np.load(allow_pickle=True), including the 'tensors-only' PIT weights file. Do not load untrusted checkpoints. A CAM Unified weights-only file should use safetensors or weights_only=True.

Replay persistence is not append-only. cam7 rewrites one monolithic pickled object array per checkpoint (about 84 KB per episode). SL4 writes .replay.pkl.gz beside latest.pt only. The agentrs Collector's JSONL sink strips messages.
Success-only replay (SL4 PPO.buffer, ContinualPPO reservoir) and EpisodicMemory evicting failures first both violate spec 11.2 ('avoid replaying only successes').

PPO-style ratios on replayed data: cam7 _rl_step applies clipped ratios to decisions from the last 96 episodes, which can be many versions stale, without validation. SL4 SIL replays successes with a PPO-family loss. Spec 12.3 forbids unvalidated stale PPO. Only unified V-trace is the validated off-policy estimator.

The agentrs async Collector marks an episode as an error and stops it if engine.version changes mid-episode. With continual weight updates this would discard most long OpenWorld episodes; CAM Unified needs behaviour-logp + version provenance plus V-trace instead.

The async Collector/engine is coupled to agentrs.econ (Task, Episode, Step, make_env, render, finish) and to chat-message LLM generation (messages, prefill, token ids). It is not wired to SessionCore.

No RMSNorm/SwiGLU/rotary/KV-cache exists. Cam7Model and EventCore use nn.TransformerEncoder(norm_first=True, activation='gelu'), recomputed over the window every act. plasticity.diagnostics assumes layer.linear1 (nn.TransformerEncoderLayer) and will break with a custom SwiGLU block.
GPU runs are not bit-reproducible (ledger: seed 3 rerun 0.041 vs 0.31 mean). Cam7 act() frozen evaluation re-seeds eval_gen and ctx_rng in reset_context.

SessionCore.tools() returns None when the tool list has not changed (signature = count + last name); call tools(force=True) to always get the list. Tool specs are about 79 KB of JSON for 141 tools, too large to feed raw every step.

spawn_env_server uses the multiprocessing 'fork' context and prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG). Combining it with CUDA initialised in the parent is unsafe; create the servers before touching CUDA, or use the hub/socket form.
The SL4 default LLM server model is Qwen/Qwen3-14B (llm-serve default), which is not in the local HF cache; only 0.6B/1.7B/4B are. TextBackbone loads with local_files_only=True.

gotchas: ow_* families are not registered when you only import crucible.worldgen: generate({'family':'ow_market'}) raises KeyError. Call crucible.load_all_modules() or crucible.scale.pool.ensure_registered() first, then ensure_modules([...]) on the spec's modules.
World.create's default world_id is 'w-' + spec.hash()[:12], identical for identical specs. With a store, a second world gives StoreConflict. Always pass a unique world_id.

The in-memory event log grows without bound until params.log_retain (default 2,000,000 events), at about 1 KB per event: ow_market adds about 2.5-3 MB RSS per simulated day, and 365 days peaked at 1.4-1.6 GB. Long CAM lifetimes need overrides params.log_retain set small plus a store (SQLite), and the observation cursor must not fall behind the window, otherwise visible_events/events_range raises ProtocolError when there is no store.
Per-actor rate limit params.max_actions_per_hour = 240 in ow_market. A learner that issues many calls per simulated hour gets rate-limit rejections, so the clock must advance.
Endowment defaults differ: admin.join 0, CrucibleEnv/CrucibleParallelEnv 0, League 2,000,000, WorldEnv and WorldPool job 3,000,000 cents. An unfunded CAM seat cannot pay compute or fees.

WorldEnv's default reward is the change in the actor's own bank balances (cents), not independent revenue. Endowments, transfers and loans move it. Pass objective='module:factory' (RewardContract protocol) for verified rewards.

The two self-play systems are different. crucible/selfplay (4.0) handles only numeric hidden-mechanism 'rig' worlds through the Learner contract (fixed 61-d observation / 12-d action; positions mean nothing across worlds). Text/tool economy self-play is training/league.py (3.0, Policy factories, sequential matches in one process, a fresh world per match). Neither runs matches across processes. Distributing is up to the caller, for example WorldPool jobs.
KernelSelfPlayEnv.reset() raises unless t==0, so build a new env or fork. SelfPlayEnv shares compiled engines in a module-global cache _ENGINES (cleared above 256 entries).

Neither RolloutFarm nor WorldPool has a central inference server. make_policy runs inside every worker, so a GPU CAM model would be loaded once per worker. Options: AsyncRunner/batch_group in one process, policy_scope='worker', or write a pipe/RPC proxy Policy.

Supervisor/WorldPool use the 'spawn' start method: driver scripts need `if __name__ == '__main__':`. MAX_WORKERS (default 8) is read from CRUCIBLE_SCALE_MAX_WORKERS at import time. The Supervisor refuses to start if free pids < 8*n+64.

The docs' scale numbers assume 48 vCPUs or an 11.52-core quota. Here the quota is 23.04 cores, and throughput flattens past about 16-22 workers (25.9 → 29.1 sim-days/s). The world kernel is single-threaded by design, so scale comes from replicas.

Sandbox RLIMIT_NPROC=512 is per uid (nobody) and so shared across all sandboxed programs of all worlds in the container. With many parallel worlds each holding up to sandbox_max_workers=24 service workers, the total can hit this cap. This is inferred from the code, not measured.

This host runs kernel 5.15 with Landlock ABI 1: the Landlock TCP deny layer described in SECURITY.md/modes.py is not active, and seccomp alone blocks sockets (verified). The sandbox shares the host kernel; VM-grade isolation is unavailable (no /dev/kvm, no gVisor).

Only tool-submitted code is sandboxed. The learner's own process, the Crucible kernel, trusted genesis incumbent code and the LLM backends run unsandboxed in the caller's process. The 'no real internet' guarantee for those comes from construction (no tool opens a socket; HFBackend uses local_files_only=True; servers bind 127.0.0.1), not from OS enforcement.

Sandboxed programs may import only numpy (APPROVED_PACKAGES): CAM-generated code cannot use torch or other libraries. Limits per job: job_wall_s 10 s (code.run timeout_s ≤ 30), mem 1536 MB, 200 files, 256 KB per file, 64 KB output.
Sandbox workdirs accumulate in /var/tmp/crucible-sbx when worlds run in-process outside WorldPool (42 dirs observed, a few from my runs). WorldPool cleans them per pid.
Snapshots (.blob) and the WorldPool .agents side files are pickles: load them only from trusted locations.

The dashboard is read-only and unauthenticated: middleware rejects non-GET, and the CLI refuses non-loopback without --allow-remote. The /experiments page renders curves only for format 'crucible-experiment*' (curves[pol][...]['points']) and Elo/score for 'crucible-league*'; any other format shows only the markdown report.

Scripted policies (Builder etc.) keep their plan in generators and have no state_dict, so a WorldPool resume restarts them from scratch. Builder picks the weakest need from market.browse, so it works in ow worlds even though their needs are named gen.<family>.<hash>.

The tool list in OpenWorld is large: 200 tools, 112 KB of JSON. LLMPolicy truncates it to tool_chars=9000. Tools needing free-form content (code.commit files, contracts) cannot be filled by the structured ActionTemplates used by the superlearner and RL adapters.

League forces params.cost_model='deterministic' (counts executed Python lines; undercounts numpy work). WorldPool digest determinism also needs the deterministic cost model when code executes. ow_market already uses cost_model deterministic.
Event payloads must never be mutated after emit; the hash chain breaks on replay (a documented kernel contract). New CAM-side world modules or routines must deep-copy.
reuse_recommendations: Insert CAM Unified as an ordinary participant: admin.join with a neutral handle and an endowment, then drive it through an agents.base.Policy subclass (act(obs, tools) -> {'tool','args'} or None, observe_result, state_dict/load_state_dict for checkpoints). Run it with Runner or AsyncRunner next to scripted Builders/Composers and LLMPolicy seats. The in-world minds, founders, NPC firms, workers and lenders and the 4,000 consumers are the 'existing Crucible behavioural actors' required by spec section 13.6.
For several CAM seats or checkpoints in one world on one GPU, use AsyncRunner with a shared batch_group implementing act_batch, so wake-ups at the same simulated second share one forward pass.

For historical checkpoints and opponent sampling, reuse training/league.py League (add_policy with factory=..., parent=..., heldout=True; PFSP sample_opponents; Elo/TrueSkill; evaluate_heldout keeps held-out results out of training stats) on ow_* families. Outcomes come from measure_agent on authoritative state.

For distributed actors (Workstream F), reuse scale/rollout.py RolloutFarm: versioned parameter blobs via publish(), per-trajectory param_version/staleness, persistent world keys routed to a fixed worker, backpressure. Use scale/pool.py WorldPool for checkpointed long world jobs. Missing pieces you have to add: a central inference path and a GPU-aware policy scope.
Use WorldEnv (or CrucibleEnv with reset_mode='fork') together with goals.contracts.RewardContract or GoalVerifier for verified rewards. Do not rely on WorldEnv's cash-delta default.

Log decisions with training/trajectories.py RecordingRunner/step_records (crucible-traj/1 JSONL or NPZ) as the base record, extended with CAM fields (predicted outcome, uncertainty, retrieved memory ids, policy version, update refs) under a new format tag, e.g. 'cam-unified-trace/1', so ImitationDataset and the dashboard trajectories page still read the shared fields.

For Part 18, extend dashboard/app.py rather than starting over. make_app returns a FastAPI app, so new GET routes (learning curves, checkpoint diffs, world-model calibration, real vs imagined, compute) can be added with app.add_api_route, reusing svg_lines/svg_bars/svg_graph and the sections.html kinds. Link per-world drilldowns to the existing /w/<id>/trace, /agents, /society and /chain pages for lifetime case studies.

Use storage SQLiteStore plus make_anchor/verify_anchor to persist and certify each CAM lifetime's world log. Use analytics.trace.timeline/explain/causal_chain to build the 'retrospective readable summaries from actual recorded actions' in spec section 18.1.

For numeric facility tasks and multi-seat cooperation/competition, wrap the CAM numeric controller as a research.learner.Learner and reuse selfplay SelfPlayEnv/Individual/SelfPlayLeague/modes, plus audit.classify_pair to separate collusion from value creation.

Read /workspace/agentrs/superlearner/src/superlearner/selfplay/arena.py: an existing Arena with several CAM learners in one persistent Crucible world, segment-wise online updates and counterfactual idle-participant runs. It is the closest prior art to CAM Unified multi-agent OpenWorld lifetimes.

Size parallelism to the 23-core quota, not 48 CPUs: about 16-22 single-threaded world processes give 26-29 sim-days/s on ow_market with light agents. Leave quota for the learner. Memory is not binding at about 60-120 MB per world process for short horizons, as long as log_retain is bounded.
gaps: No central or remote batched inference service for actors in other processes. RolloutFarm builds the policy inside each worker; AsyncRunner batch_group works only within one process.
No distributed self-play for text/tool economies. training.league.League plays matches sequentially in one process; selfplay/ (4.0) covers only numeric rig mechanisms.

No experience format fields for CAM's internals (predicted outcomes, uncertainty, imagined trajectories, retrieved memories, fast-belief changes, learning-update references). crucible-traj/1 records only observation, tools, action, result, reward and events.

The dashboard has no learner-side views: current checkpoint, experience counts, learning curves beyond the crucible-experiment format, world-model calibration, retention/transfer metrics, real vs imagined outcomes, parameter/gradient changes, compute consumption per learner. There is also no plugin hook; routes must be added to the returned app or make_app must be edited.
No gradient, parameter-change or representation tracking anywhere in crucible (the Part 18.2 items).
Nothing marks a principal as a 'CAM' participant for analytics. The /agents page lists active non-NPC persons; League seat handles are deliberately neutral.
No VM-grade isolation on this host, and no Landlock network layer (ABI 1). The learner process itself and in-process trusted code are not sandboxed.
Sandboxed agent code can import only numpy, so CAM-generated programs cannot use other libraries inside the world.
LLM social minds (Tier-3) have been tested only with the test double, not with a real model at scale. Concurrent reasoning LLM agents at scale were never run (SCALING.md).

There is no OpenWorld adapter for CAM 7.0 or Unified (CAM7_LEDGER: 'Experiment 4 (OpenWorld) ... not started'). Existing adapters are for CAM 2.0 (integrations/agentrs_cam2.py) and the superlearner (integrations/agentrs_sl.py).

read:ow_goals_worldgen.summary: Crucible's goals are GoalContract objects (crucible/src/crucible/goals/contracts.py). Each is a typed JSON predicate over registered metrics (goals/metrics.py), with a horizon, an optional count of consecutive daily checks it must be sustained for, an endowment and a world (family, seed, overrides, optional warmup_s). A contract never names a strategy. Verification is independent: GoalVerifier keeps its sustain counters outside the world and reads state only through metric functions. Success is never credited if the predicate is already true at begin(). RewardContract adds potential-based shaping (lambda*dPhi) plus a one-time success bonus, so cycling earns nothing. Five procedural goal families exist (revenue, recruit, service, solvency, outperform), each with 4 levels. Three more are mined from running open worlds by goals/taskgen.py (relieve_loss, adoption, visibility). lab_improvement is listed as a held-out family but has no generator. Anti-self-dealing lives in metrics.revenue_analysis: related parties are excluded (self, member orgs, orgs sharing a member, founders even after they leave, the services they operate). Payments pulled under a delegation and loan principal are excluded. Escrow counts only when released to the real buyer or poster. Money returned through any chain is netted out by Edmonds-Karp max-flow from the agent's group to its payers. Households (simulated consumers) count as independent. Agents cannot create persons. evaluation/audit.py reports exploit attempts but does not change rewards. Worlds come from worldgen.generate(config, seed) -> WorldSpec over 24 named families plus 50 mech_* facility families, tagged train/val/test/dev. They include classic economies (bazaar, ...), open firm-mind economies (open_digital, open_tight_compute), industrial worlds (open_industry, open_mixed, ...), generated-category OpenWorld economies (ow_market, ow_frontier, ow_composite, ow_heldout, ow_works) and the engineering_lab pair. Test families hold out whole need formats, category families and mechanisms, not just seeds. Mined tasks are split by a hash of (family, seed), and the held-out file is SHA-256 sealed. The synthetic internet has about 19 built-in hosts (identity, bank, mail, forum, search, docs, code, issues, cal, support, ads, market, cloud, biz, contracts, jobs, plus open-world caps/ops/deal/gov/net/appdb/wf/use/rig). Agent code is real: code.run, code.test and every request to an agent-deployed service run as CPython subprocesses under uid nobody with rlimits, Landlock (ABI 1 here, filesystem only), seccomp (no sockets, exec or fork) and wall timeouts, talking to the kernel over a JSON-lines pipe (crucible_sdk.call). Only the landlock-seccomp backend is available on this host. Scripted competent controls exist to calibrate feasibility: Builder, Employer, Composer, BountyHunter, CapacityInventor, PeakPricingInventor, PlacementBroker, MaintenanceInventor, ProcessResearcher, SiteAuthor, EvidenceAggregator, ExampleInductor. TaskValidator runs idle, random and competent policies in forks, then near-miss checks, then a difficulty estimate. I measured that a 'revenue >= $10k per 30 days, sustained 7 daily checks, within 90 days' contract (OW-1) is reached by the scripted Builder in 25-35 simulated days on bazaar, ow_market and open_tight_compute seed 1. Evaluating a goal predicate costs microseconds to 2 ms; fork-based battery metrics cost about 0.13-0.2 s. The real cost is simulating the world: 0.2-2.2 s per simulated day, so a 90-day OW-1 episode is about 1.5-3.5 min plus the learner's own inference, and a full validation of one task costs about 3x horizon of simulation. On the spec's task list: OW-1 is directly supported (needs an operating-profit predicate). OW-2 and OW-3 are partially supported (adoption, use-ledger, lab and relieve_loss metrics exist, but there are few validated tasks and some metric bugs). OW-4 is partially supported (scheduled shocks and sector liveness, but no agent-level detection/recovery metric). OW-5 has worlds but no industrial goal family or scripted industrial control. OW-6 has self-goals and an autocurriculum, but no anti-trivial filter or learning-progress objective. OW-7 has contracts, deals, jobs and self-play modes, but no packaged joint-utility goal.

gotchas: CRUCIBLE_SANDBOX_DIR must be traversable by uid nobody. Pointing it under the session scratchpad (/tmp/claude-0 is mode 0700) makes every code.run and deploy fail with 'SandboxUnavailable: sandbox failed to start ... Permission denied'. The Builder then silently never deploys (host 'none', progress 0). Use the default /var/tmp/crucible-sbx (exists, mode 711).

quality_margin_vs_incumbents counts as incumbents only sellers in the `npc_firms` table. That table is EMPTY in every firm-mind world (open_* and ow_*: ow_market 0, open_mixed 0, open_tight_compute 0; bazaar 8, ow_tiny 2). In those worlds the margin is just the agent's own quality (measured 1.0), so the `outperform` goal is trivially satisfiable there and not a valid test.

quality_margin_vs_incumbents runs the hidden battery through the normal capacity path in a fork. When the agent's instance is overloaded or being redeployed that hour, its quality reads 0 (I measured -0.993 once and +0.007 at other times for the same best-tier service). Sample it at several times or bypass capacity.

In ow_* worlds the scripted Builder is privileged: it deploys tier_source(need, best_tier(need)), the category's hidden-rule reference solver. Its success there is an upper bound, not a fair competent control. The non-privileged control for generated categories is usefulness.agents.ExampleInductor (exemplified categories only).
GoalContract.budget (e.g. max_actions) is not enforced anywhere. Only the kernel param max_actions_per_hour (240) limits actions.

Runner advances the clock by a fixed dt per round and ignores each action's cost_s. With dt=3600 the agent gets exactly one action per simulated hour (2,160 over 90 days). Use AsyncRunner or the gym env time_mode='cost' for realistic time costs.
Daily checks and sustain sampling happen only when RewardContract.step_reward or GoalVerifier.daily_check is called. LIMITATIONS says 'sustained goals are watched only at harness steps'.

bindings() only considers orgs where the actor's membership role == 'owner'. $host is that org's deployment with the most service_requests_ok over 7 days. An agent acting through an org where it is only admin or member gets no credit.

independent_revenue's default netting window equals the measurement window. LIMITATIONS: colluders whose two legs fall outside the window both get credit, and a one-way payment from a colluding unrelated agent is indistinguishable from a purchase. For multi-agent runs pass netting_window_s = run length.

Households count as independent revenue. In bazaar-type worlds all OW-1 revenue is household demand. There is no 'recurring' or repeat-customer notion beyond a 30-day window sustained over k daily checks.
There is no profit or operating-margin metric. ops.operating_result and the ops_days journal exist only in worlds with the `ops` module (open_*/ow_*, not bazaar/tiny). rig_net covers facilities only.

goal_suite and the curriculum use only is_economic() families (civ + consumers). Industrial worlds (open_industry, open_scarce_energy, open_fragile_suppliers, open_perishable) are excluded, and mech_* are marked economic=False.

load_all_modules() registers the ow_* and mech_* families, so families('train') / goal_suite('train') now include ow_market, ow_frontier, ow_works and the mech_* train families. Pin world_families explicitly to avoid picking them up by accident.

Adversarial content (adversary) and generated sites (webgen) are installed but produce nothing unless configured through overrides.module_config. trust_boundary.assess returns adversary_present False otherwise.

TaskValidator.default_controls has no control for revenue/recruit/service/solvency/outperform, so validating those goals fails with 'no feasibility witness' unless you pass controls. Near-miss binding swap picks an unrelated firm from the `minds` table, so in non-open worlds the binding check is skipped (None).
code.run returns ActionResult.ok=True even when the program failed. Look at result['ok'] and result['error']. Exceptions in lab controllers return only type and location, never the message.

The default cost model ('measured') makes forks and reruns non-bit-reproducible. ow_*/open_* families set cost_model='deterministic' (line counting), which undercounts native work (numpy) and so gives cheap compute to agents that exploit it.
Validation selection effect: a task is accepted only if the competent control solves it, so 'competent N/N' is true by construction. Mined relieve_loss tasks were 0/7 accepted, adoption 1/3.
reuse_recommendations: OW-1: build the contract directly as a GoalContract with independent_revenue(principal='$org', window_s=30d, netting_window_s=horizon) >= 1_000_000, sustain_checks >= 7, horizon 90d. Calibrate with the Builder (it succeeds on bazaar/ow_market/open_tight_compute s1 in 25-35 days), and with ExampleInductor in ow_* worlds for a non-privileged witness. Add an operating-profit leaf before claiming 'positive operating economics'.

Use evaluation.harness.run_goal / RewardContract as the external objective for CAM. Use GoalVerifier status (success, progress, streak) as the evaluator signal only, never as a CAM input. Keep evaluator objects outside the world, as the code already does.

Reuse TaskValidator (with explicit controls) to gate every CAM task: idle/random shortcut forks, competent-control witness, near-miss. Reuse calibration.classify for failure taxonomy, and audit.integrity_report + trust_boundary.assess on every run.

OW-2: compose a predicate from capability_adopters(min_active_s>=3d) and/or use_independent_requests / use_customer_value / use_verified_quality on the agent's $host, in ow_frontier/ow_heldout. Use use.probe (paid hidden-instance acceptance lab) as the in-world feedback channel. Do not use quality_margin_vs_incumbents in firm-mind worlds until it is fixed.

OW-3: use engineering_lab / engineering_lab_heldout with a GoalContract over lab_improvement_vs_baseline(window_h) >= threshold. GREEDY_SOURCE gives +0.75-0.84, so a threshold around 0.3-0.5 is feasible. relieve_loss mined tasks (loss_events <= 0.7x reported rate + revenue_from) are a second, harder source.

OW-4: use families with scheduled shocks (expensive_compute_open_distribution day 25 compute_shortage, entrenched_incumbents day 15 entrant, labor_rich_fragile_infra day 10 reliability, novel_needs day 12 new_need, bazaar day 20 pref_drift), or overrides.module_config.shocks.events. Use longrun.inject_shock for bankruptcies and outages, and lab daily drift/shocks. Measure agent-level recovery yourself (independent_revenue before and after).

OW-5: train on ow_market/bazaar/open_digital, transfer to open_industry/open_scarce_energy/open_perishable, mech_tech_* (techsys has no train families) and engineering_lab_heldout. Generic metrics (independent_revenue, rig_net, lab_improvement_vs_baseline) work there even though goal_suite skips them.

OW-6: use the selfgoals module (goals.propose) as CAM's self-goal action and GoalSampler as the external held-out probe schedule. Evaluate periodically with goal_suite('val') / locked_test_goals in forks of the persistent world.

OW-7: use contracts/deal deliverable predicates (check_predicate_scope requires metrics with declared subjects), jobs (hiring independent NPC developers, Employer control), Composer (paying other firms' APIs), the recruit goal family (independent_members), and selfplay.modes 'cooperative' / 'mixed_motive' on rig facilities.

For throughput, run worlds in separate processes (SCALING.md: 16 replicas about 6.9 sim-days/s aggregate). Fork from snapshot_blob (40 ms) for paired evaluations, with cost_model='deterministic' so forks are exact.
gaps: No operating-profit or margin metric registered (needed for OW-1 'positive operating economics'). ops_days and operating_result exist only in ops-enabled worlds and are not exposed as a @metric.

No 'recurring revenue' or repeat-customer metric for need-format services outside the `use` module (use_retained_customers only covers `use` categories). OW-1 'recurring' must be approximated by a 30-day window sustained over k daily checks.

quality_margin_vs_incumbents and the 'outperform' goal family are invalid in firm-mind worlds (open_*, ow_*), because incumbents are not in npc_firms. A hidden-battery comparison against mind-run incumbents needs a fix (read listings of all non-related sellers or civ firms).
No generator for the declared held-out goal family 'lab_improvement' (HELDOUT_GOAL_FAMILIES lists it, GOAL_FAMILIES does not). Lab goals must be hand-built.

No goal families for industrial worlds (is_economic excludes them) and no scripted industrial entrepreneur control to calibrate an industrial revenue/profit task. Only ProcessResearcher and MaintenanceInventor exist, and they sell knowledge or maintenance. OW-5 feasibility calibration is therefore missing.

OW-2 'novel software adoption': only firm minds adopt capabilities (via switchback trials, documented as noisy). Of the mined adoption tasks only 1/3 had a feasibility witness. Simulated consumers only pay for need formats that already exist (a new category is not adopted unless a world declares it latent or new_need). No validated multi-seed adoption task set exists.

OW-4: no agent-level measure of 'detects change / revises understanding / recovers'. Longrun liveness is per sector, not per focal agent. Shocks are pre-scheduled per family, and there is no generator of randomised shock schedules for economic families (only lab shocks are random, via shock_p).

OW-6: self-goals have no anti-triviality filter (e.g. 'cash >= 0' is accepted and 'met'), and no learning-progress or intrinsic objective grounded in prediction error. GoalSampler's learning progress is over external arms only. The self-goal experiment was never run (LIMITATIONS).

OW-7: no packaged goal measuring jointly produced utility with independently controlled participants. NPC firms do not negotiate contracts or alliances with agents beyond employment, lending and licence buying. Free text never influences NPC decisions. Self-play cooperation exists only on rig mechanisms, not in the full economy.

No browsing population: simulated people do not visit web sites (LIMITATIONS, Crucible 3.0). Audience, content and community tasks have no real demand side, matching the spec's 'important environment limitation'.
No VM-grade isolation on this host (landlock ABI 1, so no Landlock network rules either; seccomp blocks sockets). Any workload requiring min_isolation above 'process' is refused.
GoalContract.budget (action and compute budgets) is not enforced by run_goal or the verifier.

The scripted Builder in ow_* worlds uses hidden-rule reference solvers. There is no non-privileged competent business control for specified or experiential generated categories (ExampleInductor covers exemplified categories only), so OW-1/OW-2 feasibility in ow_heldout cannot be witnessed fairly with existing controls.

read:llm_integration.summary: Every Qwen model in the repo is loaded the same way: Hugging Face transformers 5.24 AutoModelForCausalLM (or AutoModel) in bf16, moved to cuda, eval mode, requires_grad=False, attention 'sdpa'. Nothing uses vLLM, quantization, flash-attn, bitsandbytes or any grammar library, and none of these is installed. Only Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B are local, under /workspace/.hf_home/hub, and all three finished downloading. Qwen3-14B, which superlearner's HFModel and server use by default, is NOT present. There are five integration patterns. (1) crucible/agents/llm.py: LLMPolicy plus HFBackend, a frozen chat model that writes one JSON tool call per turn as {"tool": ..., "args": ...}, parsed leniently by crucible.api.render.parse_action, which also accepts <tool_call>, fenced code and OpenAI/MCP shapes. research/llm_eval.EvalLLMPolicy adds the corrected 'v4' prompt (full catalogue, 40k-character tool budget, structured error detail). (2) agentrs/cam2/backbone.py: FrozenLLM. Mechanism A is pooled or per-token features read through forward hooks on chosen layers. Mechanism B is CAM-controlled generation: P control vectors are spliced through inputs_embeds as [ctx][P prefix][stub][target], with left padding, explicit position_ids and a manual DynamicCache decode. logprob_with_prefix is differentiable with respect to the prefix only and rescores row by row (exact=True), because padded bf16 batches drift by up to about 0.06 nats. It is fed by CAM.prefix (agentrs/cam2/model.py) and used on Crucible through crucible/integrations/agentrs_cam2.CrucibleAdapter: CAM picks the tool and the frozen LLM writes the JSON args. (3) LoRA exists only outside the OpenWorld action path. agentrs/models/backbone.LMBackbone wraps PEFT get_peft_model (r16, alpha 32, all-linear), and agentrs/econ/learner.GenPolicy uses it for Qwen3-4B with the assistant prefill '{"tool": "' in the econ domains. superlearner/cam/backbone.TextBackbone has a hand-written LoRALinear on q/v for a 0.6B embedding backbone only. (4) superlearner/llm: a frozen 14B text plus embedding service. Embeddings are the prompted last token at hidden_states[-4], centred, randomly projected to 512 dims and L2-normalised; there is a sqlite cache and a unix-socket server. grounding/executor adds schema prechecks through crucible.core.schema and a failure taxonomy. (5) agentrs/cam/hybrid: FrozenSemanticEncoder (pooled features), FrozenLLMActor (option scoring by log-likelihood under a small grammar) and LLMFrontend (few-shot text rewriting). agentrs/cam/model.py contains no LLM: it is a from-scratch CAM whose grammar masks are re-applied when training, which is the right pattern to copy for constrained decoding. Frozen-LLM results in OpenWorld/Crucible 4.0 are uniformly 0 successes. Qwen3-4B v4 gives mean score -0.0006 over 6 mechanism tasks, the same as idle; it makes valid calls but loops on one call (rig.read 192 of 192 turns, search.query 192 of 192). Qwen3-1.7B v4 scores -0.046 over 3 tasks with mostly schema errors. The 4B and 14B final challenges and the open economy all have success 0 and progress 0. The CAM2 smoke run with 0.6B: 0% success, 70% schema rejections. On the A6000, measured: Qwen3-1.7B (hidden 2048, 28 layers, 16/8 heads, vocab 151936, 1.72B params, 3.2 GB of weights) prefills 8x512 in 0.22 s (18.5k tok/s). Eager decode is CPU-bound at about 31 ms per step whatever the batch size (252 tok/s at batch 8). Static cache auto-compiles: about 18 s on the first call, then 12.3 ms per step (649 to 694 tok/s at batch 8). Soft-prefix injection through inputs_embeds, generate(inputs_embeds=...), PEFT LoRA, and LoRA together with a prefix all work, with gradients reaching the external network and none reaching the frozen weights. The cleanest path for CAM Unified: one wrapper around a bf16 Qwen3-1.7B or 4B plus PEFT LoRA, a bridge that produces K prefix vectors scaled to embedding norm, layer hooks for token states, and a custom LogitsProcessor (not prefix_allowed_tokens_fn) with precomputed GPU masks for the JSON tool-call grammar, storing the masks so the learner can rescore exactly.

EvalLLMPolicy (corrected v4 prompt), run_mechanism / run_open_economy, controls, RunStore; RUNNER_DT=1800, OPEN_DT=3600.
