Measured frozen Qwen3-4B/1.7B OpenWorld results: 0 successes on every task.
action_format_help() (the {"tool","args"} convention), parse_action (lenient parser: <tool_call>, code fences, <think>, OpenAI/MCP shapes), render_tool / render_observation.

CrucibleAdapter: Crucible tools become CAM ToolSpec objects with one 'args' JSON argument carrying inputSchema. Parsing and validation counters, step, reward contract, snapshot. smoke_run measures CAM2 with a frozen Qwen.

FrozenLLM: hook-based pooled and per-token hidden states; inputs_embeds prefix splicing (_assemble with masked_scatter); sample_with_prefix and differentiable logprob_with_prefix. The best existing template for soft-prefix conditioning.
CAMConfig(llm_hidden=2048, prefix_len=8, prefix_rank=256) and CAM.prefix(f, c_sel) -> (B,P,H): a low-rank bridge plus a learned base initialised from token embeddings, times pre_scale.
gen_prompt (the argument-writing prompt), Agent.act: CAM chooses the tool, the frozen LLM writes JSON (GEN_MAX json=96 tokens) under the prefix; behaviour logp is recomputed through the learner path.

LMBackbone: HF causal LM plus PEFT LoRA (LoraSettings r16/alpha32/all-linear). Shared-prefix KV scoring, generate_tokens returning exact ids and logprobs, token_logprobs_from_ids, pooled, gradient checkpointing.

GenPolicy and policy_backbone_cfg: Qwen3-4B bf16 with LoRA r16 all-linear, RL-trained (GRPO/PPO) to emit JSON tool calls after TOOL_PREFILL '{"tool": "' (src/agentrs/econ/rollout.py). Econ domains, not OpenWorld.
ExpertAdapters: several PEFT LoRA adapters with a learned Router, plus distill_into_shared (continual-capacity tooling). lora_rank.py: function-preserving rank expansion.
FrozenSemanticEncoder (hooked layers, mask-mean pooling, LRU cache; default Qwen3-0.6B) and FrozenLLMActor (grammar-slot choice by option log-likelihood; default Qwen3-4B).
LLMFrontend: few-shot rewriting of text into CAM tokens, greedy batched generate, left padding. ParserFrontend is the rule-based baseline.
From-scratch CAM 1 (no LLM). Its grammar-masked autoregressive action decoder caches masks and re-applies them in action_logprob: the pattern for exact constrained-decoding replay.
LLM interface; HFModel (default Qwen3-14B, not downloaded) with generate, generate_batch, generate_mixed and embed (prompted last token at layer -4, 512 dims); CachedLLM (sqlite); extract_json.
Frozen LLM server over a unix socket with batching by token budget, OOM fallback and a shared cache. RemoteLLM client, BackboneClient, connect(spec).
Program-proposal and argument-writing prompts (SYSTEM_PROPOSE, SYSTEM_GEN, gen_messages, gen_keys_messages / gen_entry_messages for entry-by-entry file writing).
TextBackbone: a trainable 0.6B embedding backbone with mode none|lora|top:k|full (hand-written LoRALinear on q/v), a gradient cache (LiveTable) and EmbedService.
GroundedExecutor: alias resolution, tool lookup, Crucible schema validation (crucible.core.schema.validate/with_defaults), loop guard, error-code-to-failure-class mapping with actionable feedback.
JSON action-program language (call/wait/if/repeat/foreach/code/use/define_tool/gen) and its interpreter: an alternative to single tool-call actions.
ObservationBatch already has text [...,M,D] and text_mask slots for pretrained token embeddings. encoders/observation.py has text_proj = nn.Linear(text_dim, d).
Documents the frozen-LLM agent, the CAM2 adapter, and measured 1.7B and 0.6B smoke numbers.
My benchmark script: prefill, decode, hidden states, inputs_embeds prefix with gradients, PEFT LoRA, trie-constrained decoding. Results in r1.json and r2.json in the same directory.

The sequence is [ctx = '<|im_start|>user
{user}<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
'][P prefix][stub = '<think>

</think>

'][tgt], left-padded with explicit position_ids = cumsum(mask)-1. Gradient flows to the prefix only.

To read the pre-norm output of layer 28, or only a few layers cheaply, use model.model.layers[i].register_forward_hook(lambda m, inp, o: store(o[0] if isinstance(o, tuple) else o)), as FrozenLLM does.

(b) Soft prefix: emb = model.get_input_embeddings(); pre = bridge(z).to(torch.bfloat16)  # [B,K,2048], scale to the embedding norm (row norm ~1.54, RMS ~0.0345 per element); e = torch.cat([emb(left_padded_ids), pre], 1); m = torch.cat([attn, torch.ones(B, K, dtype=torch.long, device='cuda')], 1); new = model.generate(inputs_embeds=e, attention_mask=m, max_new_tokens=64, do_sample=False, temperature=None, top_p=None, top_k=None, pad_token_id=151643)  # returns ONLY new tokens. Training: out = model(inputs_embeds=torch.cat([emb(ctx), pre, emb(tgt)], 1), attention_mask=..., logits_to_keep=T_tgt+1); loss = F.cross_entropy(out.logits[:, :-1].float().flatten(0,1), tgt.flatten()); loss.backward()  # gradient reaches the bridge; LLM params get none

(b') Middle insertion ([ctx][prefix][stub]) with left padding and explicit position_ids: reuse agentrs.cam2.backbone.FrozenLLM._assemble / sample_with_prefix / logprob_with_prefix (PYTHONPATH=/workspace/agentrs/src).

gotchas: transformers 5.24: output_hidden_states returns L+1=29 tensors where the LAST entry is already passed through the final RMSNorm (it equals last_hidden_state). The pre-norm output of the last decoder layer is not in the tuple; use a forward hook on model.model.layers[-1]. hs[i] for i in 1..27 is the raw output of layer i.

transformers 5.24 warns that the past_key_values kwarg is deprecated and will be removed in 5.40 ('Use `cache` instead'). FrozenLLM.sample_with_prefix and LMBackbone pass past_key_values and will break on a future upgrade.

Eager decode costs about 31 ms per step whatever the batch size (1 to 32), so decode time is set by step count, not batch. Batch as many streams as possible. cache_implementation='static' auto-compiles (an 18 s first call) and is 2.6x faster, but its greedy tokens and logprobs differ from eager after about 1 token. Behaviour logprobs used for RL must be recomputed through the learner's own forward path, as FrozenLLM.logprob_with_prefix and CAM2 agent.act already do.

In bf16, a padded batched forward's result depends on the padding length (FrozenLLM docstring: up to about 0.06 nats). For exact PPO ratios, rescore row by row without padding (exact=True) or always use identical shapes.
Logits have 151936 columns but the tokenizer has 151669 tokens, so ids 151669 and above are padding rows. Any vocabulary mask must have width logits.shape[-1] and must mask the padding rows.

Tokenizer facts: default padding_side is 'right' (set left for generation); pad is <|endoftext|> (151643); the chat terminator is <|im_end|> (151645). generation_config defaults to do_sample=True, temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95, so greedy decoding requires do_sample=False and temperature/top_p/top_k=None, as the repo code passes.

With enable_thinking=False the chat template appends '<think>

</think>

' after '<|im_start|>assistant
'. FrozenLLM.chat_ids builds this by hand without a system message. Keep prompt construction byte-identical between collection and training.

Qwen3's native tool convention, through apply_chat_template(tools=...), is <tool_call>{"name":..., "arguments":...}</tool_call>, while Crucible's is {"tool":..., "args":...}. Without constraints the 1.7B model wraps its replies (for example ```json {"tool_call": {"name": ...}}``` or {"action_control_signal": ...}), which caused the 70% schema rejections in the CAM2 smoke run. Forcing the '{"tool": "' prefill, or constrained decoding, removes this class of error.

Frozen Qwen in OpenWorld fails in two ways: the 4B produces valid calls but loops on a single call for the whole episode, and the 1.7B makes schema errors. There is no positive success baseline to beat, only controls (the scripted experimenter scores 0.13; the privileged reference 0.99).

The v4 prompts are 4.5k to 8.5k tokens and every turn re-prefills from scratch (no cross-turn KV or prefix caching anywhere). At about 18k tok/s that is about 0.3 to 0.5 s of prefill per turn for 1.7B before any decode.

Soft prefixes are powerful: a random prefix with embedding-matched RMS already derails the reply. Initialise from real token-embedding rows (CAM2 uses token_embedding_rows plus a learned scale) and keep the norm near the embedding row norm (about 1.54).

Backward through the frozen 1.7B at 8x520 tokens needs more than 12 GB without checkpointing. gradient_checkpointing_enable(use_reentrant=False) plus model.train() brings it to 4.4 GB. HF only checkpoints in training mode, which is safe numerically because Qwen3 dropout is 0.

PEFT creates fp32 LoRA weights on the bf16 base and casts activations for the LoRA path, so memory is higher than expected (2x512 step with full-vocab CE peaks at 9.6 GB). Use logits_to_keep or chunked CE and gradient checkpointing.

prefix_allowed_tokens_fn that returns list(range(V)) on unconstrained steps makes generation 4x slower. Use a LogitsProcessor that is a no-op outside constrained spans, with precomputed GPU bool masks. A forced head that ends in a space produces 'args":  {' with a double space; end forced text before the space token.

No grammar or constrained-decoding library is installed (no outlines, xgrammar, llguidance or lm-format-enforcer), and there is no jsonschema or vllm. The only JSON-schema validator in the repo is crucible.core.schema.validate/with_defaults, and it validates complete objects only.

reuse_recommendations: Build the CAM Unified language module as one class that generalises agentrs.cam2.backbone.FrozenLLM. Keep _assemble (left padding, explicit position_ids, masked_scatter prefix splice), sample_with_prefix / logprob_with_prefix (exact row-wise rescoring) and the layer hooks. Add an optional PEFT LoRA (get_peft_model, r 8 to 16, q/k/v/o and MLP) and a trainable bridge P_t = W(Z_t, G_t, B_t) that outputs [B,K,H] prefix vectors, shaped like CAM2's CAM.prefix (low-rank plus base initialised from token embeddings, times a learned scale).

(a) Hidden states: use forward hooks on the chosen model.model.layers[i] (and model.model.norm for the final normed states) rather than output_hidden_states, so only the needed layers are kept. Feed token states through ObservationBatch.text / text_mask (already in unified/interfaces.py) and text_proj into CAM's width. For retrieval-style document or tool embeddings, reuse superlearner HFModel.embed's prompted last-token, layer -4 recipe; it beat mean pooling in the repo's tool-retrieval probe.

(b) Prefix injection: place the K vectors between the context and the answer stub (CAM2 convention) or after a left-padded prompt. For sampling use model.generate(inputs_embeds=..., attention_mask=...), which returns only new tokens and was verified equal to the input_ids path. For training recompute log p(tokens) with model(inputs_embeds=..., logits_to_keep=T+1) and gradient checkpointing.

(c) LoRA: start from agentrs.models.backbone.LMBackbone / agentrs.econ.learner.policy_backbone_cfg (Qwen3-4B, bf16, LoRA r16 all-linear, '{"tool": "' prefill, exact sampled ids and logprobs) for the RL plumbing. Use peft disable_adapter() for a frozen reference or KL anchor, and agentrs/capacity/{experts,lora_rank}.py for multi-adapter routing and rank growth in lifetime learning. Keep the 1.7B as the first target: 8x512 prefill takes 0.22 s and a LoRA step 0.23 s per 1k tokens on this GPU.

(d) Constrained JSON tool calls: implement a ToolCallLogitsProcessor that forces '{"tool": "', applies a token trie over the currently available tool names (or lets the CAM pointer head pick the tool and forces its tokens), forces '", "args": {', and then decodes args under a schema-driven character-level pushdown automaton over precomputed decoded token strings. Use cheap GPU masks for value classes: digits are single tokens; string-safe tokens are those without a quote, backslash or control character; key names and enums come from tries. Validate the finished object with crucible.core.schema.validate and route execution through superlearner GroundedExecutor for feedback. Store the allowed-id sets, or make them a deterministic function of the prefix, so the learner re-applies the identical mask (agentrs/cam/model.py generate_action / action_logprob pattern).

Environment interface: reuse crucible.integrations.agentrs_cam2.CrucibleAdapter (tool to ToolSpec with the JSON schema, invalid/schema/world counters, snapshot/restore) or crucible.research.llm_eval.run_mechanism / run_open_economy for evaluation against the existing controls. Reuse EvalLLMPolicy with the V4 config as the frozen-LLM baseline arm.

Throughput: batch rollout streams into one generator (superlearner/llm/server.py batching shows how). Use cache_implementation='static' (auto-compile, 2.6x faster decode) only for collection, with logprobs recomputed by the training path. Keep cross-turn prompts short or add prefix KV reuse, because full v4 prompts are 5k to 8k tokens per turn.
